images.title: The hreflang rules in one place
images.alt: Checklist of hreflang rules: language code first, every version lists all versions, links go both ways, full URLs and an x-default fallback.
images.caption: Hreflang helps Google pick between your versions. It doesn't rank any of them higher.

items: Start with a language code like es; a region like es-MX is optional
A region code on its own isn't valid
Every version lists itself and all the others
Links must go both ways, or Google ignores the tags
Set x-default as the fallback page

images.after: What Google ignores, and what it tells you not to do
images.title: What Google ignores or advises against
images.alt: Four cards: the lang attribute doesn't set language for Google, avoid automatic redirects, add visible language links, and the hreflang report is gone.
images.caption: Google reads the visible content to decide a page's language.

items.title: The lang attribute
items.text: Google doesn't use it to detect language, but browsers and screen readers do

items.title: Automatic redirects
items.text: Avoid redirecting by IP or browser language; Googlebot crawls mostly from the US

items.title: Visible language links
items.text: Put a link to the other languages on every page and let the reader choose

items.title: No hreflang report
items.text: Search Console dropped it; check page source or use a crawler

images.title: Common hreflang mistakes and fixes
images.alt: Table of four hreflang mistakes and their fixes: missing return links, invalid codes like en-UK, cross-language canonicals and relative URLs.
images.caption: A template change can drop the tags without warning, so recheck them in regular audits.
